run_dispersion.criteria: fit {coefficients, alpha, diff_shrink, home_field_runs_adj} on the fit half of a 70% date split; on the HELD-OUT half all four must hold: (1) home win, paired Brier, non-inferiority, one-sided 95% lower bound on delta >= -0.001; (2) THE RUNLINE, BOTH SIDES, scored as the per-game SUM of the log loss on home margin >= 2 and the log loss on home margin <= -2 (equivalently home -1.5 and away -1.5; the +1.5 sides are their complements and score identically), paired, delta > 0 at t >= 1.645; (3) total over 9.0, paired log loss, delta > 0 at t >= 1.645; (4) runs both sides, out-of-sample log-likelihood per row, NB > Poisson. Moneyline is non-inferiority because diff_shrink already absorbs its calibration and NB must not be credited for beating it there. AMENDED 2026-08-09: V1 said only 'margin >= 2' and did not name a side, the first run scored the home side alone, and the side changes the verdict; see RUNLINE_SIDE_AMENDMENT. The verdict is taken from `dispersion_gate_sensitivity`, which requires the amended criterion to hold at split quantiles 0.6, 0.7 and 0.8, not from any single split.
run_dispersion.criteria_v1: fit {coefficients, alpha, diff_shrink, home_field_runs_adj} on the fit half of a 70% date split; on the HELD-OUT half all four must hold: (1) home win, paired Brier, non-inferiority, one-sided 95% lower bound on delta >= -0.001; (2) margin >= 2, paired log loss, delta > 0 at t >= 1.645; (3) total over 9.0, paired log loss, delta > 0 at t >= 1.645; (4) runs both sides, out-of-sample log-likelihood per row, NB > Poisson. Moneyline is non-inferiority because diff_shrink already absorbs its calibration and NB must not be credited for beating it there.

checks.criterion: runline (both sides, per-game sum of the two log losses), paired log loss, superiority
runs, both scoring sides, out-of-sample log-likelihood per row

run_dispersion.runline_side_note: criterion 2's estimand. `home` is the log loss on home margin >= 2 (home -1.5, equivalently away +1.5), `away` the log loss on home margin <= -2 (away -1.5, equivalently home +1.5), `both` their per-game sum. The board publishes all four prices and they are these two events; V1 of the pre-registration named no side and the first run scored `home` alone. See betting_model.RUNLINE_SIDE_AMENDMENT
run_dispersion.mode_note: forward split on season-to-date features. Both arms see the identical features and the identical fit window, so the contamination cannot favour one distribution over the other; this gate asks about SHAPE, not about skill

sensitivity.rule: the amended criterion 2 must pass at EVERY split quantile, with the other three criteria, or the gate is INDETERMINATE and dispersion stays off; a verdict that moves with the split point is a verdict about the split point
sensitivity.note: side-by-split sensitivity for the section 11a gate. `home` was the only reading the first run reported and V1 of the pre-registration did not name a side

run_dispersion.verdict_note: `passed` is the pre-registered single split under the amended criterion 2. `verdict` is the ship decision and comes from `sensitivity`, which requires that criterion to hold at every split quantile. Where they disagree, `verdict` governs and `served` follows it

feature_basis.note: schema-3 dark capture only: counts of gradable and eval games whose vintage record carried each column, said why it was null, or predates it (docs/diamond-betting.md section 5c). Nothing served reads these columns; a null is never filled from live files

vintage.note: 777 games graded on vintage features; 600 are needed before min_edge may be fitted, and the paired-Brier gate must also clear. 11 of the eval games carry no park term at all (their vintage predates the park column); the park index is NOT borrowed from the live file, which would leak the in-progress season

skill_vs_home_base.note: paired per-game Brier difference against the constant home-field baseline; positive means the model is better, and t >= 1.645 is the one-sided 95% bar

fit_window.why_not_graded: these are the games the coefficients and both one-parameter corrections are FITTED on, so scoring them would be scoring the model against its own training data; they are excluded from n_graded by construction and not by oversight

doors.top_up: _row_from_schedule reads the schedule's teams[side].probablePitcher, and overwrites the row by game_pk on every refresh

agreement.source: the stored rows of .cache/betting/completed_games.json against the cached feeds in .cache/game_feeds

equals_first_pitcher_used.source: R4 count A over the 2,197 cached feeds of the 2,200 completed games in the cache that day
equals_first_pitcher_used.denominator_note: frozen, and NOT the counts block in this same disclosure: counts is this run's rows and grows every night, this rate is R4's archive as it stood
equals_first_pitcher_used.retires_when: the tools/betting_lineup_job capture store fills and the rate can be recomputed against the probable the board actually had

starter_basis.served_board_reads: the probable listed at the nightly build, which is not this field
starter_basis.copy_repair_owed: betting_export.MODE_MEANING["vintage"], rendered on /betting/, says the listed probable comes out of the vintage snapshot. The snapshot supplies his SEM+ ratings; his identity comes from the completed-game row. Named 2026-09-17, owed, to be repaired under the copy rules in its own step
starter_basis.note: the backtest's starter is the FINAL feed's probable, so the graded pricer holds a starter the served board does not always have. Who starts is fixed before the first pitch, so this is a difference in information and not an outcome leak (plan 2026-09-11 repair 5; docs/diamond-betting.md 5j)

prob_calibration.criteria: fit (a, b) of p' = sigmoid(a*logit(p) + b) by MLE on the fit half only; on the held-out half BOTH must hold: (1) paired per-game Brier delta, identity minus Platt, > 0 at one-sided t >= 1.645; (2) paired log loss delta not worse on the point estimate (>= 0). Splits at date quantiles 0.6, 0.7 and 0.8, ALL THREE or nothing, fit half >= 100 games and eval half >= 50 or the split cannot pass. Arm 1 is the vintage-gradable sample with {coefficients, tie, diff_shrink, home_adj} refit on each fit half; arm 2 is the calibration ledger's settled canonical-side moneyline games, ACTIVE only at n >= 100, same splits and criteria in settled order. Ship requires BOTH arms; serving is moneyline only.

per_market.objective: LEXICOGRAPHIC, ACCURACY FIRST (owner decision 2026-09-05, decision 6). Per market: (1) the ACCURACY leg is paired per-game Brier and log loss on the vintage eval window against the ladder tiers, always including the market OPEN tier recomputed on the same games, and it is read FIRST; (2) the ROI leg is flat-stake ROI with the one-sided 95% lower bound `sweep_min_edge` already uses, plus expected log growth at quarter Kelly on the recorded price, per (market, rule) cell. A market may set a threshold only when its accuracy leg is NON-INFERIOR to the market open on the same games (paired Brier lb95 >= -0.002) AND its ROI leg clears an lb95 above zero at n >= 100 inside ONE (market, rule) cell. A market that fails the accuracy leg has its ROI leg REPORTED and NOT CONSULTED: a positive ROI on a market whose probabilities lose to the open is a sample, not a finding. Floors: 100 canonical games per market for the accuracy leg, 100 settled rows per (market, rule) cell for ROI. CLV is one key carrying the reason it does not exist, never a null column.

ridge_fit.criteria: fit both arms on the fit half of a date split and score both on the held-out half, with {extra-innings tie rate, diff_shrink, home_field_runs_adj} re-solved SEPARATELY for each arm on its own fit half, so a tuned incumbent is never graded against an untuned challenger. The ridge penalty is chosen inside the fit half by moneyline log loss on an inner date split at RIDGE_INNER_SPLIT_Q; the eval half is never consulted for it. At split quantiles 0.6, 0.7 and 0.8, ALL THREE or nothing: (1) NON-INFERIORITY, paired per-game Brier, ridge minus OLS, one-sided 95% lower bound >= -0.001; (2) SUPERIORITY over the literature Elo tier (tools/betting_elo, the section 6 ladder's results-only floor), paired per-game Brier, ridge better at t >= 1.645; (3) paired log loss delta not worse on the point estimate (>= 0). Fit half >= 100 games and eval half >= 50 or the split cannot pass. Coefficients and diff_shrink are persisted at every split, so a verdict that rides on one window is visible as one.

total_level.criteria: the recentre is one additive constant delta (runs) on the Poisson total mean; the margin, the moneyline and the runline are computed from the unshifted lambdas and may not move. CENTRE arm (the candidate): delta = argmin of the summed over/under log loss at the fixed line grid (7.5, 8.5, 9.5, 10.5), equal weights, over the fit half, golden-section on [-3, 3]. MEAN arm (the 2026-09-05 plan's literal candidate): delta = mean actual total minus mean model total on the fit half. Splits: the anchored served split (_vintage_cut_index) AND the date quantiles 0.6, 0.7, 0.8 of the vintage-gradable dates; every split refits {coefficients, tie_home, diff_shrink, home_adj} on its own fit half as the vintage lab does, fits delta on that same fit half, and scores the eval half. On each split's EVAL half BOTH must hold, at ALL FOUR splits or the verdict is not ship: (1) paired per-game total log loss summed over the same grid, incumbent (delta 0) minus recentred, > 0 at one-sided t >= 1.645; (2) paired per-game log loss at EACH grid line not worse on the point estimate for at least three of the four lines. Structural and asserted by test, not measured: moneyline and runline byte-identical with the flag on and off. Fit half >= 100 games and eval half >= 50 or the split cannot pass. Diagnostics, never criteria, because the market is a diagnostic target and never an input: model P(over) at the posted line minus the realised over rate on eval games with a cached open capture, and the Over/Under split of positive-edge totals on every cached slate.
